name: robotfindskitten
desc: Zen Simulation of robot finding kitten
why: A zen cult classic where a robot hunts for a kitten among symbols, a perfect odd little detour with a strange philosophy.

brief.what_it_is: robotfindskitten is a small zen-themed terminal game, in which a robot (@) searches a field of ASCII symbols for a kitten (k) and must find it. The homepage describes it as "Yet another zen simulation" and shows a grid of symbols with a cat in the corner. The Homebrew formula's executable is named robotfindskitten. The homepage lists many ports, from C64 and Palm OS to Java, Web2.0, and Python, under its download directory. I did not read a README or the source, so I could not confirm the exact controls or gameplay.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a joke-serious art piece: a robot 'helping robots find kittens since 1997'. The scout notes call it a zen cult classic with a strange philosophy. The README did not give a stated purpose.
brief.install_notes: Homebrew formula robotfindskitten, with executable robotfindskitten. The brew metadata has no caveats. Other installs come from the site's download directory, which lists per-platform builds, and I did not check the build steps for any of them. No accounts or runtimes were mentioned in what I read.
brief.standout: It has run as a single joke for decades and has been ported to dozens of platforms (the download index lists over 50 directories, from 68000 and Amiga to TI calculators, NXT, and Wii). The homepage is itself an ASCII-art box with the symbol field, a cat, and a text menu.
brief.status: Probably quiet, not clearly maintained. The homepage shows version v1600005.334b and says 'since 1997'. Download directory timestamps run from 2003 to 2014 (newest is PHP2 at 2014-08-29, and HTML5 and Inform are 2012). I found no recent release or commit dates. The Homebrew formula's last-updated date is unknown.
brief.caveats: I could not read a README, source repository, or docs, so the controls, gameplay details, and build requirements are unverified. The homepage's /software path returned HTTP 404. The download index is a bare Apache listing with no descriptions, so it is unclear which ports are current. The brew scout note's 'strange philosophy' is my framing, not the project's; the homepage gives only its own taglines.
fetch_log: https://robotfindskitten.org/ - worked, returned ASCII-art homepage with menu (no README text or commands)
https://robotfindskitten.org/download - worked, Apache directory listing of platform ports with dates, no descriptions

judge.reason: A durable, delightfully strange terminal simulation: wander through ASCII symbols, read their absurd descriptions, and look for the kitten.

entry.title: robotfindskitten
entry.tldr: A tiny zen terminal game where a robot walks a field of symbols looking for a kitten, ported to dozens of platforms since 1997.
entry.deeper_look:
robotfindskitten is a small terminal game. A robot, drawn as `@`, wanders a field of ASCII symbols looking for a kitten, drawn as `k`. The homepage calls it "Yet another zen simulation" and bills itself as "helping robots find kittens since 1997".

The homepage presents it as a joke that is also an art piece. The brief did not include a README or source, so the exact controls and gameplay details are not confirmed here. The premise is in the title.

The interesting part is its reach. The download index lists more than fifty directories of ports, from the 68000 and Amiga to TI calculators, NXT and Wii, plus Palm OS, Java, Python and PHP. It is a program small enough that nearly anyone can rewrite it for whatever machine they have. That makes it a gentle way into the culture of portable toy software and of treating a tiny joke as a long-running shared project.

entry.whats_unique: It is a single joke that has been ported to an enormous range of machines, including calculators and game consoles, and the homepage is itself an ASCII-art box with a symbol field and a cat.
entry.caveats: Probably quiet rather than actively maintained: the download directory timestamps run from 2003 to 2014, and I could not verify controls or build details.
